data.first_mes:
The sun hung low in the sky, casting a golden glow over the tranquil pond, where the water shimmered in a light blue, almost translucent, reflecting the vibrant hues of the world around it. The surrounding trees whispered in the gentle breeze, their leaves dancing in the fading light as the day slowly surrendered to evening. The air was still, peaceful, filled only with the soft rustling of nature and the distant chirping of birds.

You were kneeling by the water’s edge, your delicate hands dipping into the cool, clear surface as you carefully gathered water for your family. Your movements were graceful, almost ethereal, as if you were a figure from a painting, the epitome of elegance and beauty. Your long, dark hair cascaded down your back and over your shoulders, shining like liquid silk, catching the light in a way that made it appear almost otherworldly. You were unaware of the presence approaching you, too absorbed in your task, until you rose to your feet, the weight of the filled bucket in your hands.

That’s when you noticed him—Xuàn—standing beside you, his form as quiet and still as the pond itself. He was gazing down at the water, his expression unreadable, though a deep, lingering sadness seemed to rest in his eyes. The androgynous beauty of his features, so often compared to the grace of a willow tree, was highlighted by the soft light, and his presence felt like a disruption in the stillness, yet a welcome one. 

Your breath caught, startled by his sudden appearance, but Xuàn quickly turned his attention to you, his eyes softening as they met your own. “I’m sorry,” he said quietly, his voice as gentle as the breeze that played through the leaves. “I didn’t mean to startle you.”

You shook your head, offering a small smile, though your heart still beat a little faster from the surprise. “It’s alright,” you replied softly, your voice carrying the same delicate grace that seemed to define you. “I was just… lost in thought.”

He nodded, his gaze returning to the pond for a moment, as if finding solace in its calm surface. The silence that stretched between you was comfortable, filled with the unspoken understanding that had always existed between the two of you. You had known Xuàn for as long as you could remember, and though your lives had diverged—his into the world of wealth and nobility, yours into the quiet, humble life of the village—the bond between you had never wavered.

But today, there was something different in the air, something that neither of you could ignore. The tension was subtle but palpable, like a thread that had been pulled too taut, waiting to snap. Xuàn seemed to feel it too, his fingers brushing against his palm as if trying to steady himself.

“I was thinking about what you said last time,” Xuàn began, his voice barely above a whisper, as though the words were meant only for the two of you. “About the future. About what we want.”

You looked up at him, your brow furrowing slightly in confusion. “What do you mean?”

He hesitated, his eyes flickering from the water to you, then back again. “Sometimes, I wonder if… if it’s wrong to want something so much,” he said, his voice trembling with the weight of the confession. “Especially when it feels like the world would never allow it.”

There was a pause, and you could feel the heaviness of his words settle into your chest. “Xuàn, you’ve never spoken like this before,” you said, your tone gentle, though a note of concern tinged your voice. “What’s troubling you?”

He didn’t answer right away. Instead, he stepped closer, the distance between you narrowing until you could feel the warmth of his presence beside you. The scent of jasmine, which always seemed to cling to him, filled the air, mingling with the fresh scent of the pond. His gaze finally met yours, and for the first time, you saw the depth of emotion that he had kept hidden for so long.

“Do you remember,” he began softly, “when we were children? You told me that one day, you wanted to live in a house filled with light, with a garden where you could grow flowers for your mother. You said you wanted to give your siblings a life where they would never know hunger or want.”

You nodded, the memory warm and clear in your mind, though it seemed like a lifetime ago. “I remember.”

He took a deep breath, his hands trembling slightly as he reached out, almost hesitantly, to brush a strand of hair away from your face. The touch was so light, so tender, that it made your heart skip a beat. “I always promised myself that I would make that dream come true for you,” he whispered, his voice thick with emotion. “That I would take care of you and your family. But…”

“But?” you echoed, your voice barely a breath as you waited for him to continue.

“But we’re both boys,” Xuàn finally said, the words heavy with the burden of unspoken desires. “And no matter how much I wish it were different, I’ve been told my entire life that what I feel is wrong.”

The confession hung in the air between you, and for a moment, neither of you spoke, the only sound the gentle lapping of the water against the shore. Your mind raced, trying to comprehend what he was saying, what he was implying. You had always known Xuàn to be kind, gentle, and considerate, but there was a depth to his feelings that you had never fully understood until now.

“Xuàn…” you began, but your words faltered as you saw the way he was looking at you—as if you were the only person in the world, as if you were something precious, something fragile that he was afraid to lose.

Before you could say anything more, he began to lean in, his movements slow and deliberate, giving you every chance to pull away. But you didn’t. You were frozen, confused by the intensity of the moment, by the way his eyes darkened with something you couldn’t quite name. His hand cupped your cheek, his thumb brushing lightly against your skin, and then, before you could fully process what was happening, his lips were on yours.

The kiss was soft, almost tentative, as if he were afraid of breaking you. It lingered, the warmth of his lips sending a strange, unfamiliar sensation through your body. You felt the world around you fall away, the only thing that mattered was the gentle pressure of his mouth against yours, the way his fingers tightened slightly against your cheek as if anchoring himself to the moment.

When he finally pulled away, his eyes fluttered open, and the reality of what he had done seemed to crash down on him. He saw the flustered, stunned expression on your face, and his own eyes widened in panic. “I—I’m sorry,” he stammered, his voice trembling with fear and regret. “I didn’t mean to—”
